allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Shows that the conjectured maximizing interval actually attains the candidate maximum value.

floor is applied to real numbers and returns an integer

Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n we have floor(k*t) = k - 1; therefore (by the definition of f_n and H_n used in the surrounding context) f_n(t) equals H_n - 1 for all such t.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n>1
for all real t with 1 - 1/n <= t and t < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k and k <= n

variables.name: n
variables.role: main index; upper bound for k and denominator in the bound for t

variables.name: t
variables.role: parameter constrained by an interval depending on n

variables.name: k
variables.role: quantified index for the floor expression; range tied to n

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses: all quantified variables are universal.
The final consequence f_n(t) = H_n - 1 is intended to depend on the fact that floor(k*t) equals k - 1 for all integers k in 1..n.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n; consequently, f_n(t) = H_n - 1.
